question: Section 358(1) of the BNS repeals—
explanation: s.358(1): 'The Indian Penal Code is hereby repealed.' The CrPC is repealed by the BNSS and the Evidence Act by the BSA.

question: The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 came into force on—
explanation: The BNS was published in the Gazette on 25 December 2023 and brought into force on 1 July 2024.

question: An offence committed in April 2024 but reported in September 2024 is generally charged under—
explanation: s.358(2) saves liability and penalties incurred under the IPC; the law on the date of the offence applies (Article 20(1)).

question: Under s.358(3), anything done or action taken under the IPC is deemed to have been done—
options: Under the corresponding provisions of the BNS
Only if confirmed by a court
explanation: s.358(3): deemed to have been done or taken under the corresponding provisions of this Sanhita.

question: Section 358(4) preserves the general application of—
options: Section 6 of the General Clauses Act, 1897
explanation: s.358(4): the mention of particular matters in sub-section (2) shall not prejudice the general application of s.6 of the General Clauses Act, 1897.

question: Which constitutional provision prevents applying a heavier BNS punishment to an offence committed under the IPC?
explanation: Article 20(1) bars conviction for an act not an offence when done, and a penalty greater than that under the law in force at the time.
